overview: Both describe similar structures in different species, but homologous structures share ancestry while analogous structures share only function.
genZNote: Homologous: same blueprint, different remodel. Analogous: totally different blueprints that just happened to converge on the same design need.

aspects.label: Origin
aspects.valueA: Share a common evolutionary ancestor; structures are fundamentally similar even if functions differ.
aspects.valueB: Do not share a common ancestor; structures evolved independently to serve a similar function.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: Forelimbs of humans, bats, and whales — same bone structure, different uses.
aspects.valueB: Wings of insects and wings of birds — same function (flight), completely different structure and origin.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Homologous structures are the strongest anatomical evidence for common descent; analogous structures instead demonstrate similar selective pressures.
overlay.memoryTrick: Homologous = same origin (like 'homo' = same). Analogous = same function only, an 'analogy' not an ancestry.
overlay.commonMisconception: Similar appearance or function alone doesn't prove common ancestry — you have to trace the underlying structure and developmental origin to tell homologous from analogous.
